COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
S-24 SPLA No. 187 of 2025
With
CRLA No. 436 of 2025
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Ms. Sangeeta Adhikari Patni,
Advocate for the appellant.
The appellant seeks leave to appeal
against the judgment and order dated
17.06.2025 passed in Criminal Complaint
Case No. 3906 of 2022, Gagan Kalra v.
Mintu Yadav, by the court of Additional
Chief Judicial Magistrate/2nd Additional
Civil Judge (Sr. Div.), Rudrapur, District
Udham Singh Nagar, by which the
respondent has been acquitted of the
charge under Section 138 of the
Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
Heard.
Learned counsel for the appellant
submits that the impugned judgment and
order is bad to the extent the court has
held that there is no legally enforceable
debt on the respondent to give the
cheque. It is argued that this finding has
been recorded merely on the basis of the
fact that the witness, in whose presence
the cheque was given, has not been
examined.
Having considered, this Court is of
the view that the leave to appeal deserves
to be allowed.
Leave to appeal is allowed.
Admit.
Issue notice to the respondent,
returnable within four weeks. Steps to be
taken within ten days.

Call for the lower court record. Once
it is received, let the paper book be
prepared and given to the learned counsel
for the parties, as per rules.
List on 11.12.2025.
